lessons.claim: When measuring dt/τ_fast after the fact, use the **force-based** form (dt·|F|max/γ, with dimensionless γ=1). It is itself dt/τ_fast so there is nothing to subtract. A position difference (the rms of two snapshots) has to have the thermal noise √(2·dim·dt) subtracted in quadrature, and if the drift is at the 0.5% level of the thermal noise then in a finite sample (N=1000) the sample rms comes out below its expectation and the drift gets truncated to 0 (measured). And the worst value over the whole run has to be kept -- storing only the last guard sample gave a maximum force of 1062.9 against a last value of 244.2 kT/σ, a 4.4x difference.
